recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed unless a future work-group decision reintroduces a shared statistics datatype or a new modeling pattern.
issue_request: FHIR-31564 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification CDS issue raised for R4B. It questioned why OrderedDistribution and Statistic were treated as special data types, asked for them to appear in the special-purpose datatype diagram, and requested an Evidence example using Evidence.distribution. The final resolution instead removed OrderedDistribution because List and EvidenceReport could represent ordered distributions and requested follow-up R5 work.
initial_application: The explicit source application is commit 9545244b7167d105bd862aa06a62fea63101dec7, which removed the standalone Statistic and OrderedDistribution datatype source/pages and related build entries. Earlier related FHIR-31866 commits moved Statistic elements into Evidence and began removing OrderedDistribution from datatype lists.
additional_context: FHIR-31866 is the tightly related R5 tracker and is already represented on the combined branch by commit 7a842d2892ab4c77a26c10c1cb13f4ae93152cd9. Its Published/Persuasive resolution confirms the final model: reincorporate Statistic into Evidence, remove Statistic and OrderedDistribution data types, remove Evidence.distribution, and apply the change to R4B/R5. CDS Confluence references tie the same R5 discussion back to FHIR-31564, and Zulip searches found no conflicting OrderedDistribution discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current build-scoped source has Evidence as an active resource, defines Evidence.statistic as a BackboneElement, has no Evidence.distribution or OrderedDistribution source, and no longer lists Statistic or OrderedDistribution in the special-purpose datatype diagram.
